Oil-painting search — verdict (a negative result, robustly established)

Autonomous run. Base config confirmed active: signed-damage, dw=0.5, cw=0.5, agree=0.90. Primary pair: Vermeer Girl with a Pearl Earring photos (front/back), background removed. Second pair: Mona Lisa / real Pearl. Stopping condition (a): ran the full protocol; the new lever produced no meaningful improvement; the primary objective is at a hard ceiling.

STEP 0 — the completeness metric was NOT measuring completeness

Read from code: it was (rendered_darkness>0.05 AND subject_mask) / subject_mask — a shadow-coverage rate over the source's content region. It checks presence of shadow, not colour match; a wrong-colour render scores ~100%. Our externally-quoted "85%" was a coverage rate, not reproduction fidelity. Corrected (source-referenced), on the current best config:

metricWall AWall B
OLD coverage (what we called ~85-100%)97%99%
corrected better-than-blank (the new gate)92%99%
corrected colour-match ≤0.30 (true reproduction)57%54%

All results below use the corrected gate; true colour reproduction is ~55%.

STEP 1 — semantic face mask (implemented)

No cv2, so a deterministic skin-tone ROI (flesh-colour rule, largest upper blob, blurred) concentrates small shards on the face, blended with the gradient map at a swept weight. Wired into fragment_shards_overlap(semantic_masks, semantic_weight). Works mechanically:

STEP 2 — the result: semantic weighting does NOT help. Face is saturated.

Face recognizability is pinned at ~0.53 SSIM (girls) / ~0.36 (Mona/Pearl) across every config — semantic weight, shard count, panel count all leave it unmoved (stdev ~0.01). Multi-seed, matched control vs semantic:

configface SSIM (6 seeds)
control (sw=0)0.532 ± 0.011
semantic (sw=0.5)0.532 ± 0.013
semantic (sw=1.0)0.531 ± 0.015

Difference control→semantic: +0.004, inside the ±0.046 noise. Second pair confirms it exactly: faceSSIM 0.356 / 0.356 / 0.356 across sw = 0 / 0.5 / 1.0 — literally identical. The negative result generalises.

The face crop (bottom row) tells the story: control, semantic, and more-shards all give the same blobby flesh patch. No eyes/nose/mouth resolve at any setting.

Objective ordering (as required) and verdict

  1. Hard gates (corrected completeness ≥85% both, shards ≤300): all pass.
  2. PRIMARY face recognizability: SATURATED ~0.53 — no config beats control.
  3. Secondary global: flat ~1.3.
  4. Tertiary cryptic: 16 panels most cryptic (~0.40) — the only real differentiator, and it's the known panel-count lever, not new.
  5. Tiebreak shards: all ~90-190.

VERDICT: nothing beats the current config on the primary objective. The face cannot be reproduced beyond ~0.53 SSIM on an oil painting within 300 shards, and the semantic mask — the main new idea — does not change that. The face is colour/resolution-bound: it is a small, low-contrast, skin-toned region that the CMYK shard medium cannot resolve into features at this scale, no matter where the shards are concentrated.

Which prior flat-graphics findings survived the move to oil paintings?

prior finding (flat graphics)on oil paintings
"~55-shard optimum"Did NOT transfer — face is saturated regardless; completeness needs ~90-190 shards.
"more shards degrade SSIM / more detail helps"Reversed for the face — more shards were flat-to-worse on the face and often bust the cap. Detail does not accumulate on a low-contrast face.
"220/300 shard ceiling is the binding limit"Did NOT transfer — the binding limit here is the face fidelity ceiling (~0.53), not the shard budget. 300 is plenty; the face still won't resolve.
"panel count is the cryptic lever"Survived — 16 panels more cryptic than 12, consistent.
"K (search) fixes placement robustness"Not needed here — K=16 already 6/6 (background-removed girl makes completeness easy). Consistent: K only matters when completeness is hard.
completeness metric = "image completeness"Corrected — it was coverage, not fidelity; true reproduction ~55%.

Bottom line

The honest conclusion the whole session keeps re-confirming: this medium reproduces bold, flat, large-region imagery. An oil-painting face — small, subtly-shaded, skin-toned — is close to a worst case, and no combination of the six axes (including the new semantic mask) rescues it within 300 shards. If a portrait is wanted, use a boldly posterised version (which reads at ~30-80 shards, per the earlier flat-portrait result), not a photographic oil painting.
